sentences.text: Brachysuchus is an extinct genus of parasuchid phytosaurs, a name derived from Greek words meaning 'short' and 'Sobek'.
While Angistorhinus is considered its closest relative, Brachysuchus differed by having a much smaller rostral crest and a shorter, thicker snout.
The skull of this animal measures approximately 125 cm in length and features a distinctive hooked tip.
The lower jaws expand at the tip into a large bulge that holds the animal's largest tusks, with three tusks present on each side of this bulge.
Brachysuchus reached a length of approximately eight meters, making it significantly larger than most of its contemporary phytosaur relatives.
Evidence of new tusks forming in sockets indicates that Brachysuchus continuously regrew its teeth throughout its life.
The genus was first named by Case in 1929, with Brachysuchus megalodon designated as the type species.
Brachysuchus likely preyed on heavily armored stegocephalians rather than just fish, utilizing its powerful bite to break through their armor.
A deformed tip on one lower jaw specimen suggests Brachysuchus used significant force to break through the armor of its prey.
Brachysuchus belongs to the parent group Mystriosuchinae and is classified within the family Parasuchidae as a reptile.

Fossils of Brachysuchus are found in the Dockum Group in Texas, dating to the Carnian stage of the late Triassic period, and the animal lived between 237 and 205.7 million years ago, spanning the Carnian to Norian stages.
